_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Data Requirements for Space Debris Mitigation Assessments
summary: Specifies data the contractor must develop for Space Debris Assessment Reports and End-of-Life Plans, used by System Safety Managers to verify compliance with orbital debris mitigation standards.
use_relationship:
Data Requirements for Space Debris Mitigation Assessments to support the development of a Launch Vehicle (LV)/Launch Service Space Debris Assessment Report (SDAR) and/or Space Vehicle (SV) Space Debris Assessment Report/End-of-Life Plan (SDAR/EOLP), IAW DAFI 91-202, The US Air Force Mishap Prevention Program including implementation changes per DAFI91-202_DAFGM2023-01, Department of the Air Force Guidance Memorandum dated 13 April 2023. Data will be used by the SSC AATS/LV or by the SSC/SV Program Office System Safety Managers (SSMs) to assess if contractors' United States (U.S.) Space Force LV or SV orbital system and mission design follows National Space Policy (NSP) and, U.S. Government (USG) Orbital Debris Mitigation Standard Practice (ODMSP). (The most current version of ODMSP and DAFI 91-202 in force can be obtained at: https://orbitaldebris.jsc.nasa.gov/mitigation/ and https://www.e-publishing.af.mil/, respectively.)

This Data Item Description (DID) contain the format, content, and intended use of the information for the data the contractor will need to develop and deliver to support assessment as defined by the contract statement of work (SOW).

In this document, "SV1" refers to space vehicles, and "LV" refers to launch vehicle stage(s) that become orbital. Both SVs and LV stages are addressed. "Orbital stage components" includes items released from the orbital stage, including adapters, spacer rings, etc.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference Documents
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval dates and dates of any applicable amendments, notices, and revisions, shall be as specified in the contract.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: Data Requirements for Space Debris Mitigation Assessments shall be in contractor's format.

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: Data Requirements for Space Debris Mitigation Assessments shall contain the following:

children.title: A listing of all objects with longest dimension
children.content: greater than 5 millimeters (mm) planned to be released into Earth orbit during normal operations of the SV or LV stage, along with the following information about each object:

children.title: Rationale and a description of the necessity for release
For an LV stage
children.content: time of release from launch for LV stage.

children.title: For an SV
children.content: time of release from deployment of the SV from an LV stage.

children.title: Release velocity with respect to the SV or LV stage
Expected orbital parameters (apogee, perigee, and inclination)
children.content: after release from the LV stage or SV.

children.title: Calculated orbital lifetime until reentry into Earth's atmosphere
Material composition, dimensions, and mass of object
Total SV mass at the start of the mission
children.content: at end-of-life prior to disposal, and at any events that separate distinct phases of the mission.

children.title: Failure modes and effects analyses (FMEA) results
children.content: demonstrating that the integrated probability of explosion for all failure modes (excluding collisions) of each separate SV and orbital stage is < 0.001.

children.title: Passivation methods and processes
List of internal energy sources for the SV or orbital stage
children.content: that could cause an explosion (e.g., pressurized tanks, extra fuel or oxidizer, batteries, momentum wheels).

children.title: Description of the plan for eliminating these internal energy sources
children.content: as part of the end-of-life disposal plan.

children.title: Expected timelines
For the LV
children.content: in appropriate units, from launch time (T-0), of the following events:

children.title: Stage separation from the LV
SV separation from the LV stage
For the SV orbit transfer and flight profile plan
children.content: in appropriate units, from LV separation time (T-0), of the following events:

children.title: SV mission events that cause changes in the orbital parameters
children.content: (needed for assessment of Probability of Collision With Large Objects [PCWLO]).

children.title: End-of-Life disposal
Deployment of tether or atmospheric drag enhancement device (if equipped)
The launch trajectory/flight profile plan
Mission orbit(s) parameters (orbital elements) and time durations
children.content: spent in each mission orbit until initiation of disposal action.

children.title: Disposal orbit(s) parameters (orbital elements) and time durations
children.content: spent in each distinct phase of the disposal profile until final disposal orbit is achieved.

children.title: Planned trajectory file
children.content: if orbital elements or mass vary significantly due to frequent or constant maneuvering (e.g., during orbit transfer).

children.title: Description of orbit maintenance or station-keeping planned
children.content: for the mission duration. Describe how the orbit is going to be maintained via maneuvers or other means (e.g., electrodynamic tethers, solar sailing, differential drag control) during each phase of the mission.

children.title: Description of any collision avoidance process
children.content: that is going to be performed during orbit transfer or mission operation, including controlled disposal (reentry or on-orbit). This description includes the criteria used to determine whether a collision avoidance action is performed, e.g., threshold on probability of collision at conjunction, miss distance, whether orbit transfer maneuver uncertainty is going to be accounted for (e.g., via covariance or Monte Carlo modeling).

children.title: The SV and orbital stage components data (bill of materials)
Physical dimensions (i.e., length, height, width, mass)
children.content: of all dominant SV or LV stage components, to include: the SV bus or LV stage body, solar arrays, antennas, gravity gradient booms, adapter rings, etc.

children.title: For items that have many gaps (e.g., trusses)
children.content: effective projected area of solid portions or an accurate description of the item construction (e.g., a Computer-Aided Design (CAD) finite element model in a standard format).

children.title: Data on SV components exposed to Micro-Meteoroids and Orbital Debris (MMOD)
children.content: (not needed for LV stages):

children.title: Tabulated list of components and surfaces exposed to MMOD
children.content: that are needed to execute end-of-life disposal functionality (e.g., maneuvers, tether or sail deployment, propellant depletion), including components mounted to the inside of panels exposed to MMOD (since MMOD could penetrate through the panel and component wall).

children.title: Description of redundancy of these components
Data needed for each of these components to assess risk of damage by MMOD
Criteria for MMOD to cause failure of the component
children.content: (surface penetration depth, penetration hole diameter, number of penetrations or holes, probability of failure given a penetration has occurred, etc.)

children.title: Exposed area of each component and surface
Estimate of the fraction of the surface area
children.content: of each component and surface that is not blocked if an item is partially shielded from MMOD (e.g., less than 2*pi steradian field of view (FOV) for a flat surface).

children.title: For each single exposed surface for which penetration could prevent disposal
children.content: thickness and material (e.g., aluminum).

children.title: For each single exposed surface on which cratering could prevent disposal
children.content: (e.g., optical surfaces on sun sensors or star trackers): impact crater size or area that would prevent adequate operation of the component housing the optical surface for post-mission disposal, and material (e.g., fused silica glass, fused quartz glass, polycarbonate).

children.title: For each dual-wall or multi-wall configuration
children.content: (e.g., outer wall is shielding an inner wall whose penetration could prevent disposal): thickness and material of both walls, and spacing distance between walls. (This is needed to model the multiwall shock effect.)

children.title: For each exposed panel that is a honeycomb sheet
children.content: thickness and material of front and back panels and honeycomb panels connecting those two, and spacing distance between all panels.

children.title: For each harness or cable that is exposed to MMOD
children.content: provide a description of the cable design. For example, provide the Cable Type as described in D. Jex, A. Adkinson, J. English, and C. Linebaugh, "Hypervelocity Impact Testing of Cables," NASA TN D-7178, February 1973.

children.title: For each surface covered with multi-layer insulation (MLI)
children.content: that is exposed to MMOD, provide the mass per unit area of MLI (or description with sufficient detail to compute this) and spacing distance of MLI from covered surface.

children.title: For pressurized vessels (e.g., Composite Overwrapped Pressure Vessel (COPV))
children.content: Maximum penetration depth of vessel wall before wall rupture occurs due to pressurized fluid.

children.title: Surface orientation in the SV bus frame (i.e., surface normal vector)
Description of the SV bus attitude motion
children.content: relative to a relevant standard frame (e.g., local vertical/local horizontal frame, Earth-centered inertial frame, Sun-centered inertial (ecliptic) frame. (This is needed so that the fraction of time spent by the surface in each orientation can be determined.)

children.title: Tabulated list of items needed to assure post mission disposal reliability
Systems, subsystems, and components required to accomplish post mission disposal operations
End of mission reliability assessment results for each system, subsystem, and vehicle (SV and upper stage) component
Reliability assessments should account for failures occurring
children.content: from start of mission to completion of disposal, including the entire mission design life.

children.title: Data for uncontrolled reentry hazards assessment
Tabulated list of parts
children.content: (e.g., a master equipment list - see Example Space Vehicle Data Template on page 6) for each reentering vehicle (SV and upper stage), to include:

children.title: Mass and quantity of each part
Material composition of each part
children.content: (e.g., 2024 Aluminum, 410 Stainless Steel, Kevlar, graphite-epoxy, titanium alloy Ti-6Al-4V)

children.title: Physical dimensions for each part
children.content: (including height, width, length, wall thickness; for honeycomb panels, also include face-sheet thicknesses, honeycomb density)

children.title: Illustrations or graphics of the shape of each part
Illustrations or graphics showing placement of the parts in relation to each other
Parent/Child relationship for each part
Classical orbital elements, or best estimates
children.content: at end-of-mission for each reentering vehicle.

children.title: Expected year of reentry from an orbital lifetime analysis
children.content: assuming a nominal atmospheric profile, for each reentering vehicle.

children.title: Data for controlled reentry assessment
Description of vehicle (SV and upper stage), to include
Mass of the vehicle both pre-and-post reentry maneuver
Propulsive capability of the vehicle (thrust and specific impulse)
Delta-V and propellant mass required to accomplish post-mission disposal
Physical dimensions of the vehicle (including length, width, height, or diameter)
Illustration or graphic of the vehicle
Expected debris casualty area (Ac) associated with reentry or breakup
Reentry trajectory profile with targeted impact location
Classical orbital elements, or best estimates
children.content: at end-of-mission for each reentering vehicle.

children.title: Assessment of reentry maneuver reliability based on vehicle flight history
List of the number of successes, failures, partial failures
children.content: or significant anomalies for all prior missions of the LV.

children.title: List of previous controlled reentry attempts of the LV and associated outcomes
Data for drag enhancement devices (if equipped) other than tethers
children.content: for controlled reentry assessment, including:

children.title: Expected projected area after deployment and percent confidence level for this deployment for each device
Dimensions, shape, material, and mass of each device
Time of deployment of each device after mission start
Procedure for drag device deployment and control until reentry
Construction characteristics that make each drag enhancement device resilient
children.content: to debris and meteoroid impacts (e.g., balloon rigidization, compartments), and the expected size of debris or meteoroid that could make it non-functional as a drag enhancement device.

children.title: Expected change in ballistic coefficient/drag profile stemming from deployment of drag device
Classical orbital elements, or best estimates
children.content: at end-of-mission for each reentering device.

children.title: Data for tethers (if equipped)
Expected tether length after deployment and percent confidence level for this deployment for each tether
Width (if flat tape) or diameter (if round) of each tether
Mass of each tether or device
Tether end mass of each tether
Time of deployment of each tether after mission start
Tether construction that makes it resilient to debris
children.content: and meteoroid impacts (e.g., material, braiding, multiple strands), and expected size of debris or meteoroid that could sever the tether or make it non-functional as a drag enhancement device.

children.title: Expected change in ballistic coefficient/drag profile stemming
children.content: from deployment of tether Classical orbital elements, or best estimates, at end-of-mission for each reentering tether or device.

children.title: Data on prior on-orbit performance for each tether
Data-based rationale for each tether
children.content: on the effect(s) any prior on-orbit performance has had on the current device design.

children.title: Description of whether and how the device was
children.content: damaged or severed by debris or meteoroid impacts or by collision with another object.

children.title: Description of how successful the device was
children.content: (e.g., did it successfully achieve expected reduction in orbital lifetime?)

children.title: Description of orbit operations plan for an electrodynamic tether (if applicable)
